Subject: Latency spikes: p99 TTFT regressions since 6/9 - TerraRetail checkout

Hi Olga,

We're seeing sustained p95/p99 regressions on first-token latency (TTFT) in our checkout flows starting yesterday afternoon (6/9). The p95 is fine, but p99 jumped ~350–450ms for a subset of requests routed through west coast POPs. Attached are a few error samples and client-side TLS debug logs — you can see repeated full TLS handshakes and what looks like renegotiation attempts on the initial connection.

This is causing intermittent timeouts and cart failures during peak windows (US PST). Our ops team is fairly certain this started after an ingress cert rotation on your edge (we saw many full handshakes instead of resumed sessions). Can you escalate? We need visibility and a mitigation plan (routing or temporary fallback) — this is impacting our weekend traffic.

Attachments: terra_retail_error_samples.log

Thanks,
Sylvia Hart
SVP, Product
TerraRetail

Hi FastCDN team,

We're seeing a customer-facing regression for TerraRetail (deal TR-ENTERPRISE-2219) where first-token p99 TTFT is increasing by ~350ms for requests hitting a subset of your us-west POPs. I've attached a pcap (handshake_trace_20270610.pcap). Highlights:
- Multiple connections show full TLS 1.2/1.3 handshakes instead of session resumption; session_ticket extension absent on server responses in some flows.
- SNI in client hello appears to match expected hostname.
- Timing: full handshake adds ~300–450ms on affected connections vs resumed sessions.

Can you confirm whether there was any cert rotation, load-balancer rekey, or edge config change in us-west between 2027-06-09 18:00–21:00 UTC? If so, can you roll back or push a quick fix (re-enable session tickets, correct ticket encryption keys) while we assess?

We need:
1) Confirmation of root cause within 2 hours.
2) ETA for mitigation.
3) If you need more traces or examples, say so and I'll provide immediate uploads.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
SRE (Edge & Networking) — Redwood Inference
From: FastCDN Ops <netops@fastcdn.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Packet capture indicates TLS renegotiation/failed session resume on ingress (TerraRetail)

Jonas / Olga,

Thanks for the pcap. We confirmed an anomalous cert rotation in the us-west cluster initiated during a scheduled job at 2027-06-09T18:25:00Z. A bug in our rotation flow temporarily generated new ticket encryption keys without propagating them to all edge boxes, which caused session ticket decryption failures and a fallback to full handshakes for a subset of clients.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back the rotation at 2027-06-09T20:40:00Z.
- We deployed a hotfix to the ticket key propagation flow at 2027-06-10T02:00:00Z UTC.
- Observed partial improvement after rollback; leftover client-side caches still attempt resume with the old keys and cause occasional full handshakes while TTLs expire.

Planned next steps:
- We will force key-reissue and enable session tickets across affected POPs tonight at 2027-06-11T02:00:00Z UTC. That should eliminate most residual full-handshake cases.
- We will share a postmortem and the fix notes (fastcdn_fix_notes.txt) after the rollout.

Please send any further traces for POPs still showing p99 regressions; we'll prioritize.

Apologies for the impact — we'll follow up once the forced key reissue completes.

Regards,
FastCDN Network Ops
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

- Current status: FastCDN rolled back and scheduled a forced key reissue at 2027-06-11T02:00:00Z; we observed partial improvement but some residual p99 spikes while client caches expire.
- Impact: Customer-facing p99 TTFT regressions (~7% of sessions affected), intermittent checkout failures and elevated error rates during peak traffic. TerraRetail is at risk of revenue impact this weekend.

1) Offer TerraRetail a one-month free trial of Redwood Dedicated routing (isolated capacity) to eliminate dependency on FastCDN for the next 30 days.
2) Route TerraRetail to alternate regions / edge POPs as a temporary fallback (manual routing policy) for peak windows.
